nodes.text: When did you last speak to Daniel?

nodes.speaker: Detective
nodes.text: Did you call Daniel at 10:17 PM?

nodes.text: No. Why would I call him that late?
Present: Daniel's Phone — call log 10:17 PM, 43 seconds

nodes.text: Why did you call him?

storyEndings.title: Front page
storyEndings.text: Rohan is charged with murder. But Dev had his look at the ledger, and his story ran at dawn. By the time the court order reached the bank, a co-signatory had emptied the Hill Supply reserve. The staff of Rainwood House read about their pensions in the newspaper, and that is the only place they will ever see them.

storyEndings.title: A confession buys back a pension
storyEndings.text: Page 47 went up the kitchen chimney while Rohan was out of your sight. But you asked him about the families instead of the blow, and he wrote the account number out himself. The bank freezes the reserve at 08:40, twenty minutes before the standing transfer. Rohan is charged with murder; the pensions come home.

storyEndings.title: Ashes in the stove
storyEndings.text: Rohan is charged with murder on the weapon, the grip in the brass and his own account. But page 47 burned while he was out of your sight, and with it the only record of where the money went. The standing transfer runs at nine. Malini tells the staff herself.

storyEndings.title: The missing page restored
storyEndings.text: Motive, opportunity and method, each answered from the record. Page 47 goes to the bank with a court order and the reserve account is frozen before the morning transfer. At Rainwood House the staff finally read the books that held their future.

case.title: The Monsoon Ledger
case.tagline: Four suspects. One missing page. A door that tells a lie.
case.description: A hotel owner dies during a monsoon blackout. Search nine rooms by torch and UV lamp, break four accounts of the evening, and decide who to trust. Your choices change what survives to be found, and how it ends.
case.story: At 21:10, on a rainbound November night, Arun Jayawardene is found dead in the locked study of Rainwood House Hotel. A fallen tree has closed the hill road. His daughter says he was about to sell the hotel. His chef says the staff pensions have vanished. His financial manager has a timestamped alibi. A journalist was waiting for a meeting that never happened. You arrive with a torch, a UV lamp and a fingerprint kit. Nothing in this house is labelled for you: search the rooms, read the records for the line that matters, and catch each of them in the thing they are not saying. Be careful what you promise, and whom you let out of your sight.

victim.name: Arun Jayawardene
victim.description: A widower preparing to put the hotel into a trust. Found beside his desk with a fatal head injury.

objectives: Search every room. Some things only show under UV or powder.
Catch each suspect in what they are hiding.
Link your clues to answer the open questions.

suspects.name: Anika Jayawardene
suspects.publicInfo: Anika returned to restore the hotel her mother loved. Staff heard her argue with her father over its proposed sale.
suspects.claim: I left his study at 20:42. From 20:48 until the lights returned, I was on a video call at reception.
hiddenInfo: She took her late mother's letters from the study, not the accounts.
Her father had privately cancelled the sale that afternoon.
suspects.motive: Prevent the sale of her mother's hotel
suspects.personality: Grieving and guarded; responds to care, resents assumptions about inheritance.

objections.text: I was on a recorded video call at reception from 20:48 to 21:04. Play it.
objections.fail: The duty officer plays the recording. Anika is on camera for the whole of the death window. Whatever else she is hiding, she did not strike the blow.

suspects.name: Rohan Senanayake
suspects.publicInfo: Rohan handles wages, suppliers, and the pension trust. He tells the police that Arun had recently become forgetful.
suspects.claim: I was in the accounts office all evening. My 20:55 supplier email proves it.
hiddenInfo: He diverted pension contributions into a company he controlled.
He scheduled an email at 20:31, killed Arun at 20:54, and hid the weapon and torn page in the laundry.
suspects.motive: Silence the audit exposing stolen staff pension funds
suspects.personality: Precise and courteous until records contradict him; then tries to make the victim seem unreliable.

objections.text: My email left the accounts office at 20:55. I was at my desk.
objections.fail: Rohan's timestamp stands unanswered. On paper, he never left his desk.

objections.text: Suppose I stepped away. Nothing puts me inside that study.
objections.fail: Without something that places him in the room, the magistrate hears only a man who left his desk during a power cut.

objections.text: And why would I harm the man who employed me for eighteen years?
objections.fail: With no motive on the record, Rohan's lawyer calls it a quarrel between friends that nobody witnessed.

suspects.name: Malini Fernando
suspects.publicInfo: Malini threatened to take Arun to the authorities over missing pension payments. She brought his last tea.
suspects.claim: I delivered tea at 20:45. During the outage I stayed with the electrician at the generator.
hiddenInfo: She suspected pension theft but did not know who was responsible.
She saw someone with a green sleeve carrying a linen bundle after the lights returned.
suspects.motive: Revenge for the missing staff pensions
suspects.personality: Blunt and protective of her staff; will distinguish what she saw from what she merely suspects.

objections.text: I was holding a lantern for the electrician. His camera never stopped running.
objections.fail: The bodycam file is continuous. Malini is in frame from 20:49 to 21:03, and the tea she served was clean.

suspects.name: Dev Wijesinghe
suspects.relationship: Invited to meet the victim privately
suspects.publicInfo: Dev booked under an abbreviated name. He has been investigating the hotel's finances and refuses to name his source.
suspects.claim: I was photographing the storm from the veranda. Arun was going to give me a statement at 21:15.
hiddenInfo: He recorded Arun's argument with Anika without permission.
His time-lapse camera recorded him throughout the death window; he can surrender the original card.
suspects.motive: Turn an unproven scandal into a career-making story
suspects.personality: Wry and cautious; cooperates when asked to verify facts instead of betray a source.

objections.text: Check my time-lapse. I am in the mirror in every single frame.
objections.fail: Every ten-second frame shows Dev on the veranda, and the stair door in the reflection never opens.

clues.title: A blow during the blackout
clues.description: One edged, blunt impact to the left temple. Death between 20:50 and 21:00. The outage lasted 20:50–21:02.

clues.title: Locked does not mean occupied
clues.description: The study door has a spring latch that locks whenever it closes. The deadbolt, the only part the inside key works, was never thrown.

clues.title: A clean circle on the blotter
clues.description: Dust outlines a round, heavy object that stood on Arun's desk until very recently. It is not in the room.

clues.title: Wiped drops by the door
clues.description: Under UV, a line of wiped droplets runs from the desk to the study door and out onto the landing.

clues.title: Down the back way
clues.description: The trail crosses the landing and turns down the service stairs. Whoever carried something bloody avoided reception.

clues.title: A damp key on a dry hook
clues.description: The spare study key hangs in its place, still wet. Someone used it tonight before the official discovery and put it back.

clues.title: An appointment, not a farewell
clues.description: Arun's diary: '20:50 — R. Bring ORIGINAL pension ledger. No more excuses.' The accounts wing matters now.

clues.title: Her birthday, as always
clues.description: Arun noted that the cabinet combination is 'her birthday'. Whose, and what date?

clues.description: The memorial plaque in reception gives the birthday of Arun's late wife: the fourteenth of March.

clues.title: One-four-zero-three
clues.description: Anika gave you the blue cabinet's combination outright: 1403, her mother's birthday.

clues.title: The tea was harmless
clues.description: No sedative or poison in cup or pot. Malini's tea cannot explain a fatal blow.

clues.title: A stain that glows
clues.description: The rag in the generator room lights up under UV, but it is machine oil and brake cleaner. It has nothing to do with the study.

clues.title: Two people at the generator
clues.description: The electrician's unbroken bodycam file keeps Malini in frame from 20:49 to 21:03.

clues.title: A witnessed call
clues.description: Anika is on camera at reception from 20:48 to 21:04 without a break.

clues.title: 'I should go up and say sorry'
clues.description: A record shows someone entering the study before the official discovery: Anika ended her call at 21:04 meaning to go upstairs.

clues.title: The photographer in his own frame
clues.description: Dev is reflected in the veranda mirror in every ten-second frame from 20:49 to 21:03, and the stair door behind him never opens.

clues.title: The beneficiary behind the invoices
clues.description: Pension contributions were booked as linen bills to Hill Supply, whose sole director and signatory is Rohan Senanayake. Page 47 of the ledger is torn out.

clues.title: An email without a sender present
clues.description: The 20:55 email was written and scheduled at 20:31. Nobody touched Rohan's keyboard between 20:46 and 21:06.

clues.title: The torch never left its charger
clues.description: The accounts office torch sits in its cradle by the door, fully charged, dust on the handle.

clues.title: The missing tea weight
clues.description: Arun's blood sits under the handle of the brass tea weight, and its dented corner fits the wound.

clues.title: A grip in the brass
clues.description: Powder raises a partial palm-and-finger grip on the weight. Its ridges agree with Rohan's elimination prints.

clues.title: A cloth with two stories
clues.description: The hotel linen carries Arun's blood and green wool fibres. A fibre match supports other evidence but cannot name a wearer.

clues.title: The stolen page fits
clues.description: The torn edge fits the stub of page 47. In Arun's hand: 'Rohan — explain these transfers tonight', beside the Hill Supply reserve account number.

clues.title: A thumb in blood
clues.description: A bloody thumbprint on page 47 matches Rohan's elimination print. He handled the page after the blow.

clues.title: The sale had already been cancelled
clues.description: Arun withdrew the hotel from sale that afternoon and put it in trust for Anika and the staff. Her supposed motive is gone.

clues.title: What the landing heard
clues.description: Dev's recorder kept running: footsteps from the service stairs at 20:52, a blow at 20:54, tearing paper and the latch at 20:57.

clues.title: What the stove left
clues.description: A charred scrap of ruled ledger paper survives: '…han — explain these tra…'. The account number is gone.

clues.title: A daughter protecting a memory
clues.description: Anika admits she has her mother's letters from the study drawer. She says she took them when she left at 20:42.

clues.title: Letters by his elbow at 20:45
clues.description: Malini saw a ribbon-tied bundle of old letters on Arun's desk when she brought the tea, three minutes after Anika left.

clues.title: The weight was there at 20:45
clues.description: Malini saw the brass tea weight on the blotter when she delivered the tea. It was gone when the body was found.

clues.title: Five minutes nobody mentioned
clues.description: Anika let herself in with the spare key at 21:05, found her father dead, took the letters and let the door latch behind her. The weight was already gone.

clues.title: Rohan was sent for
clues.description: Arun called for Rohan and the original ledger at ten to nine, and Rohan got the message.

clues.title: A witness, not an identification
clues.description: At 21:03 Malini saw a green sleeve carry a linen bundle into the laundry. She saw no face, and her porters wear green too.

clues.title: 'I went to find a torch'
clues.description: Faced with the mail audit, Rohan now says he left his desk during the blackout to fetch a torch.

clues.title: Twenty minutes unaccounted for
clues.description: With the torch story gone too, Rohan cannot say where he was between 20:46 and 21:06.

clues.title: 'A temporary loan'
clues.description: Rohan admits Hill Supply is his and calls the pension transfers a loan Arun would not give him time to repay.

clues.title: 'He was alive when I arrived'
clues.description: Rohan admits he went up to the study during the blackout.

clues.title: An admission tested against facts
clues.description: Rohan admits the blow. His account matches the scheduled email, the latch, the service stairs and the hidden bundle.

clues.title: Where the money sleeps
clues.description: Rohan gave up the Hill Supply reserve account and its standing transfer. The bank can freeze it tonight.

clues.title: Smoke from the kitchen stove
clues.description: While Rohan was out of your sight, someone fed paper into the kitchen stove. Whatever lay under the laundry basket lining is gone.

clues.title: Straight to the basket
clues.description: The constable you posted watched Rohan walk directly to the laundry and lift the lining of one particular basket. It was already empty.

clues.title: The alibi was built in advance
clues.description: Rohan scheduled his 'proof' nineteen minutes before the meeting Arun had summoned him to. The email was written to cover an absence he already planned.

clues.title: The weapon came from the desk
clues.description: A heavy object stood on the blotter at 20:45 and was gone by 21:05. The killer used what was to hand and carried it away.

clues.title: Three clocks, one gap
clues.description: Camera, call and bodycam account for Dev, Anika and Malini through the whole death window. Only Rohan is unaccounted for.

clues.title: The sleeve and the fibres agree
clues.description: The bundle Malini saw is the linen from the basket, and the green fibres in it match what the carrier wore. It narrows the field; it does not name him.

clues.title: Page 47 names him
clues.description: The ledger shows where the money went; the recovered page shows Arun had found out and meant to have it out with Rohan that night.

clues.title: Burning the page was an answer
clues.description: The only person who needed page 47 destroyed is the person the surviving scrap names. Rohan was out of sight when the stove was lit.

hints.text: Rooms are not labelled. Sweep slowly: a glint means something is there. Take the UV lamp into the study and onto the landing and sweep the beam slowly: stains glow only inside it. Things inside the desk, the post tray and the basket only show once you open them.
Pressing a statement costs nothing and often gives you the fact that breaks somebody else's story. Malini saw what was on the desk at 20:45. Compare that with what Anika says she took at 20:42.
The cabinet in the records room opens with a birthday. Arun's diary says whose; a plaque in reception gives the date. A sent email proves a server was awake, not a man: read the mail audit.

On the board, link the scheduled email to the diary appointment. Search the laundry before you let Rohan out of your sight. In the laundry, compare the folded page with the ledger, then brush powder back and forth over the page and the weight.

solution.explanation: Rohan stole staff pension contributions through Hill Supply. Arun found the transfers, cancelled the sale, and summoned Rohan with the original ledger before meeting Dev. Rohan scheduled a supplier email at 20:31, then climbed the service stairs during the outage. At 20:54 he struck Arun with the brass tea weight, tore out page 47, and left through the spring-latching door. He hid the weight, linen and page in the laundry. At 21:05 Anika let herself in with the spare key, found her father, took her mother's letters and said nothing. Her call, Malini's bodycam footage and Dev's time-lapse clear all three for the fatal minutes. Malini's green sleeve points the way but names nobody; the grip in the brass and the thumb on the page do.

reveal.title: The debt beneath the books
reveal.text: Having cancelled the sale that afternoon, Arun checks the pension transfers and finds they end at Rohan's company. He arranges to give Dev the records after confronting his manager.

reveal.title: An alibi sent in advance
reveal.text: Rohan queues the supplier email for 20:55. Later, its timestamp will appear to place him at his desk. The server keeps the earlier scheduling event.

reveal.title: Four people in the dark
reveal.text: The storm cuts the power. Anika stays on her recorded call, Malini holds a lantern for the electrician, and Dev stands in his own camera's reflection. Rohan carries the ledger up the service stairs.

reveal.title: The page worth more than a life
reveal.text: Arun refuses another delay. Rohan strikes him with the brass tea weight and tears out the page that names him. His bloodied thumb leaves the print that will undo him.

reveal.title: The door closes
reveal.text: Rohan wraps the weight in a tablecloth and pulls the door shut. The spring latch catches. The deadbolt is never turned: the key inside never made the room impossible to leave.

reveal.title: A bundle, not a face
reveal.text: As the lights return, Rohan pushes the bundle into a laundry basket and the page under its lining. Malini glimpses a green sleeve, and for a while tells nobody.

reveal.title: A daughter at the door
reveal.text: Anika lets herself in to apologise and finds her father on the floor. She takes her mother's letters, lets the latch catch behind her, and five minutes later 'discovers' him with Malini.
